primitives.name: Spatial Qualia Isomorphism
primitives.verbatim_quote: The numbers on a row of houses, the initial letters of a set of words, have no intrinsic kinship with points of space, and yet they are the conditions of our knowledge of where any house is in the row, or any word in the dictionary.
primitives.assumptions: Qualia are abstract symbols (numbers/letters) that lack inherent spatial properties but serve as indexing mechanisms for spatial location.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when the mapping between abstract qualifiers and physical locations fails, leading to spatial disorientation.

layer2.mapping: Maps the abstract-to-concrete indexing problem in perception to feature hashing in Bayesian machine learning and state representation in conformal prediction.
layer2.telemetry: Neural mislocalization errors, perceptual illusions, or systematic biases in sensorimotor integration.

primitives.name: Peripheral Color Modification
primitives.verbatim_quote: We see the sky as bright blue all over, the modifications of the blue sensation being interpreted by us, not as differences in the objective color, but distinctions in its locality.
primitives.assumptions: Objective color varies across retinal positions but is subjectively perceived as constant; only the perceived location changes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Subjective constancy breaks down under extreme peripheral viewing, leading to apparent color shifts.

layer2.mapping: Derives a kernel that transforms raw sensory inputs into stable spatial coordinates, analogous to conformal prediction's calibration of empirical distributions.
layer2.telemetry: Consistency metrics for visual processing pipelines, ensuring that spatial features remain invariant to low-level sensory variations.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is the "grounding problem": how do qualitatively distinct sensory impressions (like colors or tones) acquire spatial meaning? The primitives formalize this as a many-to-one mapping from non-spatial qualia to spatial coordinates. In GSI, this maps to feature extraction where categorical tags must reliably predict outcome probabilities. In GSE, it corresponds to state estimation where sensor readings (qualia) must be mapped to actionable states. The key failure mode is when the mapping becomes non-invertible, leading to catastrophic mislocalization or misclassification.
